summary: Frontend re-verification of iteration_19 badge-clear fix. Regression checks PASS (intensity scaling 2x on textfx-static-neon writes text-shadow blurs 8/16/36/72px; sunset writes background-clip:text; anim-shimmer injects @keyframes wdtfx_shimmer_* + inline animation; badge appears with Sparkles for neon/sunset/shimmer and gains MousePointerClick after hover-lift; hover-clear removes MousePointerClick). BADGE-CLEAR FIX IS BROKEN: after textfx-clear the [data-testid=layer-fx-<id>] badge STILL remains visible (Sparkles marker), identical to the iteration_19 defect. No console errors across all flows.

ui_bugs.issue: New value-aware regexes are still false-positive after textfx-clear due to regex backtracking. Verified with real state html captured from React fiber for the affected element: html contains exactly one 'text-shadow: none' and one '-webkit-text-stroke: 0' occurrence (and 'background-clip: border-box'), yet /text-shadow:\s*(?!none)[^;"']/i.test(html) === true and /-webkit-text-stroke:\s*(?!0(px)?[;"'\s])[^;"']/i.test(html) === true in the browser. Cause: '\s*' is greedy but backtracks to zero-width; after 'text-shadow:', \s* first eats the space then the lookahead sees 'none' and fails, but the engine backtracks \s* to empty so the lookahead is re-evaluated at the position of the space (' none') where the next 4 chars are ' non' (not 'none') and the negative lookahead succeeds, then [^;"'] consumes the space => spurious match. Same failure mode for the -webkit-text-stroke rule against ' 0;'. Net effect: layer-fx-<id> badge does NOT disappear after Clear text FX, exactly the behaviour iteration_19 flagged.

action_items: Rewrite fxOf regexes to anchor the negative lookahead against the whitespace, e.g. text: /text-shadow:(?!\s*none[;"'\s])/i AND /-webkit-text-stroke:(?!\s*0(?:px)?[;"'\s])/i AND /background-clip:\s*text/i AND /animation:\s*wdtfx_/i. Alternatively, parse the inline style value robustly (style.getPropertyValue) or, cleaner still, change TextEffectsPanel.clearFx to REMOVE the properties from the inline style instead of writing placeholder ('none'/'0'/'border-box') values so the property name simply isn't in the string.
Add a unit-level assertion for fxOf on a known-cleared style string so this regression cannot recur.
critical_code_review_comments: Negative lookaheads combined with a quantifier that can shrink to zero-width (\s*) are unsafe. Either force the whitespace to be part of the lookahead ((?!\s*none...)) or drop \s* from before the lookahead entirely.

TextEffectsPanel.clearFx neutralises effects by writing placeholder values ('text-shadow':'none', '-webkit-text-stroke':'0', 'background-clip':'border-box', 'animation':'none'). Prefer to DELETE these properties from the inline style so downstream detectors do not have to encode value-awareness at all.

success_rate.frontend: 83% (5/6 spec items pass; badge-clear defect persists)

seed_data_creation: Ephemeral: Large Header block added via dblclick on block-cmp-header-lrg; first canvas-el-* selected on canvas.
context_for_next_testing_agent:
Iteration 20 - re-verify of iteration_19 badge-clear fix.

PASS: intensity scaling still works (200% neon writes text-shadow with blurs 8/16/36/72). Sunset gradient still writes 'background-clip:text' and keeps Sparkles. Shimmer injects '@keyframes wdtfx_shimmer_*' + inline 'animation:' shorthand and keeps Sparkles. Hover-lift adds MousePointerClick to layer-fx badge; hover-clear removes it while Sparkles remains.

FAIL: textfx-clear STILL leaves layer-fx-<id> visible. Real state html (captured via React fiber for element id, header inline style: 'padding: 24px 32px; ... color: inherit; -webkit-text-fill-color: currentColor; text-shadow: none; background-image: none; -webkit-background-clip: border-box; background-clip: border-box; -webkit-text-stroke: 0; background-size: auto; animation: none; letter-spacing: normal; transform: none') is CORRECTLY cleared, but LayersPanel.fxOf's regex still returns text:true because '\s*' backtracks to zero width and the negative lookahead is bypassed. Verified in-browser: /text-shadow:\s*(?!none)[^;"']/i.test(html) === true and /-webkit-text-stroke:\s*(?!0(px)?[;"'\s])[^;"']/i.test(html) === true for this cleared html.

Suggested regex: /text-shadow:(?!\s*none[;"'\s])/i and /-webkit-text-stroke:(?!\s*0(?:px)?[;"'\s])/i . Or make clearFx delete properties.

Zero console errors across all flows. No pytest file created (frontend-only).
rca_of_the_issue: The iteration_19 fix intended to make fxOf value-aware, but the pattern 'text-shadow:\s*(?!none)[^;"']' contains a greedy-but-shrinkable '\s*' BEFORE the negative lookahead. Regex engines backtrack: after '\s*' initially matches the space and the lookahead against 'none' fails, the engine reduces '\s*' to zero-width and re-evaluates the lookahead at the position of the space, where the next 4 chars are ' non' — the negative lookahead succeeds (correctly, because ' non' != 'none'), and '[^;"']' happily consumes the space. So the regex reports a match even though the only text-shadow value in the string is literally 'none'. The '-webkit-text-stroke' rule fails the same way against ' 0;'. Fix by moving the whitespace inside the lookahead: /text-shadow:(?!\s*none[;"'\s])/i and /-webkit-text-stroke:(?!\s*0(?:px)?[;"'\s])/i, or (cleaner) delete the neutralised properties from inline style in clearFx.
